demand_findings: 42,127 clickstream searches at KD 3, which is the lowest difficulty against the highest volume of any record on this site. The demand splits in a way the SERP does not serve: 'tesamorelin' and 'egrifta' are drug queries, while 'tesamorelin bodybuilding', 'tesamorelin benefits' and 'tesamorelin weight loss' are asking about a use no trial has studied. Every measured query is informational.
h1: Tesamorelin: what the trials measured, in whom, and what happens when you stop
dek: An approved drug, approved for one thing: excess visceral abdominal fat in people with HIV on antiretroviral therapy. Every trial below was run in that population. The pivotal trial reported that the fat came back, and this page says so in the trial's own words.

queries.heading: What tesamorelin is, and the one condition it was approved for
What dose did the trials use?
queries.boundary: One dose runs through almost every trial of this compound. It was not chosen for body composition in healthy people.

queries.heading: Egrifta, and what the approval actually covers
What the trials measured, and how much changed
queries.boundary: Each figure below is an outcome a trial measured in people with HIV and abdominal fat accumulation. None was measured in healthy adults.

queries.heading: What side effects and safety signals the trials reported
What happened when treatment stopped
queries.boundary: The pivotal trial followed people past the end of treatment and reported the result plainly. It is the single most important sentence about this compound and it is missing from every page currently ranking for it.

queries.heading: Bodybuilding and anti-ageing use, and what evidence exists for it
queries.boundary: No trial in this record's ledger gave tesamorelin to a healthy adult for muscle, ageing or general fat loss. What follows is what circulates, reported as circulating.

information_gain: The only page that leads with the sentence the pivotal trial actually wrote about stopping: that the visceral fat reduction does not persist beyond treatment. Every page currently ranking omits it, and it is the one fact that changes what the compound is for. It is also the only page that frames the whole evidence base by the population it came from, people with HIV and antiretroviral-associated abdominal fat accumulation, and states in the same breath that no trial in this ledger gave tesamorelin to a healthy adult for muscle, ageing or general fat loss, which is what most of the measured demand is asking about. Third, it separates the approved indication from the circulating uses rather than letting a drug approval imply evidence for a use nobody tested.
serp_format_rewarded: Drug-information pages with H3-heavy structure, no tables and no citations, plus a vendor product page of eight words at rank 2. A cited page with a trial table and a named reviewer has no like-for-like competitor here. The difficulty score of 3 is believable rather than an artefact.
open_actions: The FDA label for Egrifta sits at rank 7 for the head term and rank 5 for the dosage query, and could not be retrieved: this sandbox reaches Europe PMC but not accessdata.fda.gov, dailymed.nlm.nih.gov or clinicaltrials.gov. The approval facts on this page come from ChEMBL and from the trials, not from the label.
Neither pivotal trial abstract declares a ClinicalTrials.gov number, so no registration table is possible for this compound from Europe PMC alone.
